receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

First, do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 16 and lives with me here in the UK. I'm wondering if I can still claim Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Since Alex is 16, you may still qualify for Child Benefit, but it depends on his current situation.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training? For example, is he attending school, college, or an approved training program?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is! Alex is in college doing his A-levels at the moment. He's still living at home with me while he studies.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great! Since Alex is 16, in college doing A-levels (which is approved education), and living with you in the UK, this is a positive indicator for your eligibility.

Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

Do you or your partner (if you have one) have an individual income over £60,000 per year? This won't affect your eligibility to receive Child Benefit, but it may mean you need to pay a tax charge.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, my income is well below £60,000, so that shouldn't be an issue.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! And just to confirm a couple of final details:

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else claimed it since he turned 16?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me - I'm his parent and he lives with me full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:
- Alex is 16 and in approved education (doing A-levels at college), which means you can continue to receive Child Benefit for him as long as he stays in approved education or training and is under 20 years old
- He lives with you in the UK, so you meet the responsibility requirement
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- Your income is below £60,000, so you won't have to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge

You can continue claiming Child Benefit for Alex while he remains in education or approved training, up until he turns 20 (or until he leaves education/training, starts working 24+ hours per week, or starts claiming certain benefits in his own right).

If you're not already claiming, you can make a claim for Child Benefit. If you're already claiming and were concerned about his eligibility after turning 16, you can continue to receive it as long as his circumstances remain the same.
